shared_threat_model.unauthenticated_by_default: Flask app in mlflow/server/__init__.py:41-46 registers all REST routes (handlers.get_endpoints()) with no authentication middleware; /get-artifact, /model-versions/get-artifact, /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/upload-artifact, /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/gateway-proxy are all reachable without credentials (server/__init__.py:70-106).
second_order_db_sources: CreateExperiment (POST /api/2.0/mlflow/experiments/create) accepts attacker-controlled artifact_location; the only validation is validate_query_string (mlflow/utils/uri.py:459-464) which blocks '..' in the query component only — scheme/host/port/path are unrestricted (handlers.py:578-596).
Run artifact roots inherit the experiment artifact_location (sqlalchemy_store.py:471, 486), so run.info.artifact_uri is attacker-influenced DB content (handlers.py:1255, 1319).

CreateModelVersion (handlers.py:1626-1650) accepts an attacker-controlled source URI; _validate_source (handlers.py:1590-1621) rejects only local/file URIs and relative paths — http/https remain fully allowed.
shared_threat_model.scheme_dispatch: get_artifact_repository (artifact_repository_registry.py:57-74, 100-101) dispatches on the URI scheme; http/https -> HttpArtifactRepository constructed with the raw URI; ArtifactRepository.__init__ stores self.artifact_uri (artifact_repo.py:45-46).
shared_threat_model.host_control_mechanism: HttpArtifactRepository._host_creds = _get_default_host_creds(self.artifact_uri) (http_artifact_repo.py:38-40); _get_default_host_creds returns MlflowHostCreds(host=store_uri, ...) (tracking/_tracking_service/utils.py:141-153) — the artifact URI IS the request host. rest_utils.http_request builds url = f"{cleaned_hostname}{endpoint}" (rest_utils.py:104-105); strip_suffix only removes a trailing '/', no urljoin, no host allowlist, no scheme check, no private-IP blocking, no redirect re-validation. requests follows redirects by default (allow_redirects not set anywhere on these chains in this tree).
shared_threat_model.protections_observed: validate_path_is_safe (path traversal only), _validate_source (local/file model sources only), validate_query_string ('..' in query only). None neutralizes URL host/scheme control on the modeled chains. _is_servable_proxied_run_artifact_root (handlers.py:190-226, 554, 950, 1261, 1665) diverts http/https/mlflow-artifacts roots to the local serving repo ONLY when the server runs --serve-artifacts (default off).

alerts.sink: requests.request(request_type, f"{target_uri}/{gateway_path}", json=json_data) (handlers.py:1143) — real outbound HTTP request
codeflows: request.args/request.json (handlers.py:1132) -> args -> gateway_path = args.get('gateway_path') (1134) -> f-string URL -> requests.request arg (1143)
alerts.q1_source_is_attacker_request_field: Yes: request.args (GET) / request.json (POST) on the unauthenticated route /ajax-api/2.0/mlflow/gateway-proxy (server/__init__.py:99-101). Entry reachable when MLFLOW_DEPLOYMENTS_TARGET is set (admin env, handlers.py:1127).
alerts.q2_real_propagation_to_request_url: Yes: gateway_path is concatenated into the request URL (handlers.py:1143).
alerts.q3_url_processing_changes_target: No urljoin/base-URL normalization; simple f-string f"{target_uri}/{gateway_path}". The prefix target_uri is fixed, and the attacker part always follows a '/', so the attacker cannot change host, port, or scheme — only the path (and via '?'/'#' the query/fragment) of a fixed destination.
alerts.q5_control_scope: path (+query/fragment) on a fixed admin-configured host. No host/port/scheme control. Exploitability limited to proxying arbitrary paths/verbs to the internal deployments gateway (possible gateway-side auth bypass / response disclosure), which is not destination-control SSRF. Redirects are followed by default, but the first hop is admin-chosen; no attacker-controlled redirect source was identified on this chain.
alerts.q6_protections: Target host fixed by admin env var; no other validation of gateway_path (it may contain '..' — path traversal within the gateway).
alerts.q7_trusted_fixed_url: Partially: the destination is an operator-configured service, not an attacker-chosen remote resource.
alerts.q8_static_reachability: Route is unauthenticated and registered unconditionally; sink execution is real. But per CWE-918 host-control criteria the destination is fixed.
alerts.q9_contamination: None: real HTTP sink, no file:/parse-only/test/diagnostics content.
alerts.rationale: Genuine unauthenticated proxy with attacker-controlled PATH on an admin-FIXED destination (MLFLOW_DEPLOYMENTS_TARGET). Under a strict CWE-918 threat model (attacker influences the network destination host/port/scheme) this is path-only and does not constitute SSRF; it is a gateway-proxy abuse issue. Residual risk noted above. Matches the query-generation notes' own concern (§7 item 2: 'attacker controls only the path on an admin-fixed host').

codeflows: run.info.artifact_uri (handlers.py:1255/1319) -> get_artifact_repository -> self.artifact_uri.split (117) -> url (118) -> _get_default_host_creds -> host_creds -> http_request (125)

alerts.q8_static_reachability_and_conditions: Sink execution is doubly gated: (a) log_artifact only calls _try_multipart_upload when MLFLOW_ENABLE_PROXY_MULTIPART_UPLOAD is enabled — default False (environment_variables.py:303-305) — and the file is >= MLFLOW_MULTIPART_UPLOAD_MINIMUM_FILE_SIZE, default 500MB (environment_variables.py:481-483, http_artifact_repo.py:47-55); (b) the only unauthenticated server entry to log_artifact (upload-artifact handler) caps the request body at 10MB (handlers.py:1241-1245), which can never meet the 500MB threshold. No other server-side entry logs a >=500MB artifact. Therefore under both default and plausible configurations the sink is not reachable from the unauthenticated surface.
alerts.rationale: The taint model and host control are correct, but the full source->sink execution path requires a non-default admin opt-in (MLFLOW_ENABLE_PROXY_MULTIPART_UPLOAD=true) that still cannot be satisfied through any server request entry due to the 10MB upload cap vs the 500MB threshold. Kept uncertain rather than fp because the gating is configuration-dependent, not a model artifact; if a future entry or configuration satisfied both conditions it would be a likely_tp.

pyvul_real_vulnerability_hit.commit_message: Add env var to disable redirects again (#10673)
pyvul_real_vulnerability_hit.pre_fix_code_verified: The analyzed tree matches code_before exactly: _get_http_response_with_retries (request_utils.py:160-190) has no allow_redirects parameter, no MLFLOW_ALLOW_HTTP_REDIRECTS read, and ends with `return session.request(method, url, **kwargs)` at line 190. Because allow_redirects is never set, requests follows redirects (including cross-origin 30x) by default — the SSRF-via-redirect behavior this commit fixes.
hitting_alerts: alert 8 (mlflow/utils/request_utils.py:190): sink is EXACTLY the patched line inside the patched function `_get_http_response_with_retries`; 3 of its 4 codeFlows show attacker-controllable (second-order) artifact-URI host control reaching this sink via HttpArtifactRepository._host_creds -> rest_utils.http_request -> url -> _get_http_response_with_retries.
alert 9 (mlflow/utils/rest_utils.py:109): the same URL being passed into the vulnerable function one frame earlier.
alerts 1-3 (http_artifact_repo.py:64/88/104): the upstream wrapper calls (http_request) whose URLs converge on the vulnerable function.
pyvul_real_vulnerability_hit.entry_chain_matches_vulnerability_descri: The exploitation pattern in the commit description (creating a model version with an http/https source, and artifact locations using http/https) is present and unauthenticated in this tree: CreateModelVersion allows http/https source (handlers.py:1590-1650, _validate_source rejects only local/file/relative-path sources), and /model-versions/get-artifact (server/__init__.py:76-78) fetches it server-side via get_artifact_repository (handlers.py:1672) -> HttpArtifactRepository -> http_request -> _get_http_response_with_retries -> session.request, with redirects followed. The alerts' codeFlows use the equivalent run-artifact-URI entry (CreateExperiment artifact_location -> run artifact root, handlers.py:1255/1319), also unauthenticated.
pyvul_real_vulnerability_hit.coverage_nuance: The Augur alerts hit the vulnerable function via DIRECT host control (the artifact URI is the request host), so the redirect-specific variant (fixed destination + attacker-driven 30x re-targeting) was not needed to produce the hit. A pure redirect-chain model (response-driven taint) was deliberately not modeled per the query notes (§6), but this does not affect the hit: the same sink line is reached with a fully attacker-controlled URL. Additionally, requests' default redirect-following at this sink is itself part of the vulnerable behavior fixed by the commit.
pyvul_real_vulnerability_hit.conclusion: The real CWE-918 vulnerability (SSRF via redirect-following / attacker-controlled artifact URLs in _get_http_response_with_retries) WAS hit by the formal Augur Pass 3 alerts — specifically alert 8 at the exact vulnerable function and line, corroborated by alerts 9 and 1-3.

overall_conclusion.statement: CodeQL 分析成功，且本轮命中 10 条正式 CWE-918 污点路径告警（ruleId py/augur/mlflow/pass3-ssrf），非空结果、非诊断查询。
overall_conclusion.summary: 5 likely_tp（artifact-URI 主机控制链：log_artifact PUT、list_artifacts GET、_download_file GET、request_utils.py:190 session.request、rest_utils.py:109 URL 传递，全部经未认证入口默认可达，且 _get_http_response_with_retries 为真实漏洞修复点）；2 likely_fp（gateway-proxy 仅固定主机上的路径控制；delete_artifacts 无服务器端可达入口）；3 uncertain（multipart upload 三个 sink，污点链真实但被默认关闭的环境开关与 500MB/10MB 尺寸矛盾阻断，实际不可达）。无 file: 本地读取、URL 仅解析、测试代码或诊断查询混入造成的错误计数。
overall_conclusion.strongest_finding: Alert 3 (http_artifact_repo.py:104): unauthenticated /get-artifact or /model-versions/get-artifact with an attacker-chosen http(s) artifact location / model-version source makes the tracking server GET an arbitrary URL and return the response body to the attacker — full SSRF read primitive; the same chain reaches the redirect-following sink fixed by commit 8174250f.
